I have farmed these same 6 mu in Quzhou for 50 years, and I finished high school back in the day, so I can read the fertilizer labels and do the math on N-P-K. My soil has gotten thin over the decades — we are on the North China Plain, loam soil, low organic matter — so I have to feed it properly or the yields drop fast. I split my land right down the middle: 3 mu for wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu for stevia. Stevia is my main income crop — last year dried leaves sold for 6 yuan per jin, while wheat was only 1.1 yuan. But I keep the grain rotation because my wife and I need the flour, and it stabilizes my income if the stevia price falls.

For winter wheat, I plant an improved variety from the county supply store — probably Liangxing 77 or something with good lodging resistance. Before planting in early October, I rotary till and spread 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, the 18-22-5 formula. That gives me about 9 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 1.5 kg potassium per mu from the basal. Then at jointing in late March, if the color looks a bit yellow, I topdress with 25 kg of urea per mu, which is another 11.5 kg nitrogen. I would rather put down a little too much than risk a bad harvest — wheat is our staple. I irrigate four times: winter irrigation once after planting, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling in spring. The well pump costs electricity, but wheat pays the bills.

Summer maize goes in within two days of wheat harvest in mid-June. The season is short, so I use no-tillage and plant hybrid seed — Denghai 605 or Nongda 372, one bag per mu at about 50 yuan. All fertilizer goes in the furrow at planting: 80 kg of 28-6-6 compound per mu plus 15 kg urea. That totals about 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, once right after planting and once at the big-flare stage in July. The summer monsoon usually brings enough rain for the rest.

Stevia is planted in mid-April with bought seedlings — 8,000 plants per mu at about 200 yuan. I rotary till twice to loosen the soil because stevia roots need good aeration. Basal fertilizer is 80 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu, and I topdress twice with 10 kg urea per mu during the growing season. Total nutrients come to about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Stevia leaves are what we sell, so insects are the enemy — I spray insecticide seven times and herbicide twice through the season. I irrigate five times because stevia cannot handle drought stress. If I manage it right, I expect 550 kg of dried leaves per mu.

My wife and I are both getting old, so we do the light work and hire local labor for stevia transplanting and harvest — maybe 10 days total at 150 yuan per day. My total input cost runs about 4,500 yuan for the year. That is real money, but the stevia should bring in over 10,000 yuan, and the wheat and maize keep us fed. I am not changing anything major this year — last year worked, and at 68 I do not take risks.
